newsitem.title: USA: Florida consumer confidence unchanged in March.
newsitem.headline: Florida consumer confidence unchanged in March.

text.p: Florida's Consumer Confidence Index held steady at 96 for March, unchanged from February, University of Florida economists said Tuesday.

Consumers' perception of their own financial status rose dramatically to 95 in March from 88 in February. But that was offset by a decline in their perception of business conditions nationwide, which fell to 94 in March from 100 in February.

"Consumers who were more upbeat about their current financial situation report wage increases and better jobs as the reason," said Chris McCarty, survey director of the University's Bureau of Economic and Business Research.
Fears about the national business picture may be well founded, university economist Dave Denslow said.

Each month since October, more survey respondents have reported pay hikes. If workers nationwide are enjoying similar gains, that makes it likely the Federal Reserve will continue raising interest rates to reduce the threat of inflation, Denslow said.
"That would be bad news for Floridians who have run up their credit cards but good news for retirees who may collect more from their savings," he said.

Among employed consumers, 55 percent reported business activity was higher in March than a year ago, an increase of six points from February. Thirty-six percent of employed respondents expected their companies to hire more employees in the next six months, up from 31 percent in February.

The monthly survey was based on telephone interviews with 879 randomly selected Florida adults and has an error rate of three points. The index uses a base year of 1966, with numbers above 100 indicating consumers are more confident than they were then, and numbers below indicating lesser confidence.
